tool.name: Call window haplotypes
tool.description: read whole haplotypes off spanning reads and name them by their own content
tool.command: ## The specimen id becomes column 1 of the calls and the row id of the sheet, so it ## defaults to the collection element identifier rather than a dataset number. #set $eid = str($input.element_identifier) #if $eid.endswith('.bam') #set $eid = $eid.rsplit('.bam', 1)[0] #end if #if $specimen and str($specimen).strip() #set $spec = str($specimen).strip() #else #set $spec = $eid #end if ln -s '$input' 'input.bam' && ln -s '${input.metadata.bam_index}' 'input.bam.bai' && pyeuk call-haplotypes --bam 'input.bam' --ref '$ref' --specimen '$spec' --bed '$windows' --min-span $gates.min_span --min-reads $gates.min_reads --min-freq $gates.min_freq --denoise-edits $gates.denoise_edits --denoise-ratio $gates.denoise_ratio --out '$calls'

param.name: ref
param.label: Reference the BAM was aligned to

param.name: windows
param.label: Windows
param.help: From 'Define haplotype windows'. Must be the same windows for every specimen.

param.name: specimen
param.label: Specimen id
param.help: Leave blank to use the collection element identifier.

param.name: min_span
param.label: Minimum spanning reads for the window
param.help: TOTAL fully-spanning reads required before a window is called at all, applied before any haplotype is examined. A read must cover every base of the window, so this is not coverage: a window can sit under 2000x coverage and have 19 spanning reads. Derived by holding BAMs and windows fixed and sweeping only this value on the Cyclospora 2018 cohort -- 24 to 42 is a flat plateau at ARI 0.9737 with one specimen misassigned, and 44 drops to 0.7536 with ten. The old default of 50 was an undocumented round number on the wrong side of that cliff. This gate is harsher on MIXED specimens: k co-infecting genotypes split the spanning reads k ways, so a mixture needs k times the depth of a clonal sample to pass it.

param.name: min_freq
param.label: Minimum haplotype frequency
param.help: This is a HAPLOTYPE frequency -- the fraction of spanning reads carrying that whole string. It is a property of one haplotype, unlike per-site allele frequency, which is a sum over every haplotype carrying that site.

param.name: denoise_edits
param.label: Denoise: fold strings within this many differing positions
param.help: 0 disables. A window string is a whole molecule, so one sequencing error creates a NEW haplotype rather than perturbing an existing one; folding a rare string into a much more abundant neighbour collapses that error cloud. Default 1 is set from a Cryptosporidium mixture titration with KNOWN proportions: off detected 110/112 mixture components at mean minor-haplotype purity 0.294, 1 edit detected 112/112 at 0.434, 2 edits reached 0.556 but fell back to 110/112, and 3 edits to 79/84. More aggressive folding buys purity by losing genuine minor components, which is the worst failure this tool can have.

param.name: denoise_ratio
param.label: Denoise: abundance ratio required of the neighbour

tool.help:
Only reads whose alignment covers an entire window are counted, so each haplotype is a complete observation on one molecule rather than an inference across molecules. Identical strings are collapsed and counted; there is no assembly.
Each haplotype is named by how it differs from the reference over that window (HGVS-like, 1-based within the window), so no curated nomenclature file is needed. A string identical to the reference is named ``=`` -- an ordinary haplotype, which is what keeps "amplified and reference-identical" distinguishable from "not amplified".
Read frequency is reported per haplotype. A mixture appears as several haplotypes in one window, which is what per-site variant calling cannot represent.
